name: royal double street lamp, 3/4 top-down: square stone pedestal (top face seen from above), iron post with gold bands and a gold star finial, a curled crossarm with a crowned lantern hanging at each end (warm lit glass)
label: beodeul_city/capital/capital_lamp_double

answer.evidence: The main body is the stone pedestal (rows 36-45, 14 px wide). Its top face is the pale band at rows 36-39, where the post base enters it. The lightness steps down at rows 40-41 (L 197, then 176), which marks a front edge, and the front face runs from there to row 45 with a blue emblem. The top is only about 4 rows with a soft edge, so this is a borderline reading. The lanterns have sloped blue crown roofs at rows 14-19 that end in a gold eave line, which counts as a top surface (c). The thin post and crossarm are slender structure with no visible top. The star finial is decor.

styleAnswer.evidence: The closest reference is prop-lamp-crook, a thin post with a single lantern and only 14 colours in total. The candidate has more structure: a stone pedestal with a visible top face, a banded post, a star finial, a curled crossarm and two crowned lanterns with lit glass. It measures 13 visible tones per full tile, against 9 for the hedge and 17-20 for the stall and well. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. Dark edge pixels are 55% near-neutral, which I read as mixed: some outline is near-black, as on the lamp-crook reference (100%), and some leans tinted. Each material ramp has about 3-4 steps (stone, iron, gold, glass), a little below Beodeul's 5-6, but the shading is not shallow. Placed next to the references, the piece does not look thinner or more sticker-like than the lamp reference.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts are fine: 13 visible tones per tile (hedge 9, stall 17, well 20), 0% near-flat coverage, and 23 colours overall. It is richer than the thin prop-lamp-crook, which has 14 colours and a 100% neutral outline. By eye, though, each material gets only about 3-4 steps. answer.evidence: The pedestal is 14 px wide and its top is a light stone band on rows 36-41 that shades from L=219 down to L=176, so it reads as a top face seen from above. The post enters this top at rows 36-37. Below it, rows 42-45 are the darker front face, with a blue and gold inset. The lantern roofs are sloped blue planes (rows 12-17) above gold eave bands (rows 18-19), which counts as evidence (c). The crossarm is a thin beam and the post is a vertical shaft, so neither needs a top surface. The star finial is decor.

styleAnswer.evidence: Measured facts are decent: 13 visible tones per tile (references 9-20), 0% near-flat coverage, and 23 distinct colours in total. Those numbers come from a small, dense object, so they don't prove richness. By eye, the stone pedestal and iron post are shaded with only about 3-4 steps, against 5-6 on the well and stall. The gold bands and lantern crowns are mostly one tone plus a highlight. The outline is mixed: 55% of dark edge pixels are neutral, and the dark rim around the lanterns and pedestal reads as a uniform near-black sticker line. The reference well and stall use tinted, material-toned darks instead. The candidate also has little grain or per-stone texture on the pedestal, where the well shades its stones one by one. It is clean and readable, and the lit glass is a good touch, but it sits below the Beodeul bar on shading depth and outline craft. When in doubt, fail.
